title: Vintage Gibson Les Paul Special Value Guide By Year
description: Vintage Gibson Les Paul Special values by year, including TV Yellow originals and 1970s reissues, with condition notes and photos from my guitar archive.
h1: Vintage Gibson Les Paul Special Value Guide
alt: Front of a TV Yellow single-cutaway Les Paul Special with two black P-90 covers

faqs.q: What Is A Vintage Gibson Les Paul Special Worth?
faqs.a: A clean original 1955 to 1959 TV Yellow Special has a guide range of $12,000 to $19,000. A 1959 cherry Special sits at $7,500 to $14,000. The annual table separates later guitars; condition, original parts and the case affect an individual appraisal.

faqs.q: Is A TV Model The Same As A TV Yellow Special?
faqs.a: No. The TV Model belongs to the one-pickup Junior family, while the Special has two P-90 pickups. TV Yellow is also a finish on the Special. I identify the model before applying a price range.

faqs.q: Why Is There No 1975 Les Paul 55 Row?
faqs.a: Les Paul 55 is a model name, not a 1955 manufacture date. A guitar represented as a 1975 example needs its serial, pots and construction checked alongside the surrounding reissue years. I can appraise it individually; the gap in this table doesn't establish that none were built.

faqs.q: Why Do Some Years Share A Price Range?
faqs.a: Several years can share an era range. That doesn't make every guitar from the period worth the same amount. I assess condition, finish and configuration before narrowing the appraisal.

faqs.q: How Does A Headstock Repair Affect Value?
faqs.a: A repaired Special needs comparisons with similar repairs and originality. The quality and extent of the work affect the result. The size of the deduction depends on the repair and the remaining original parts.

faqs.q: Does A Refret Make A Special Nonoriginal?
faqs.a: A quality refret preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise original guitar. It removes museum-quality status. Neck reshaping and fingerboard replacement are different alterations.

faqs.q: Should I Restore The Guitar Before An Appraisal?
faqs.a: Send photographs of its present condition first and keep any removed original parts. Leave the finish, hardware and wiring as they stand for the initial review.
